heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P requires a hardened steel nozzle and extruder gear upgrade alongside a draft enclosure to handle Bambu ASA-CF safely and prevent severe warping. Once upgraded, it reliably achieves print speeds up to 179 mm/s constrained by a safe 15 mm³/s volumetric flow limit at 268°C.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with liquid glue or glue stick as a protective release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap Maximum Volumetric Speed to 15 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent under-extrusion at high print velocities.
Set Part Cooling Fan to 0% min and 20% max with 80% exhaust chamber/aux fan disabled to prevent thermal shock and catastrophic layer delamination.
Configure a 5mm outer brim with a 0.1mm brim-object gap to stabilize sharp corners against draft-induced bed lifting on the open-frame P1P.
Enable Scarf Joint Seams under Quality settings to conceal carbon fiber seam bulging and reduce stringing zits during layer transitions.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe corner lifting and bed detachment
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: The open-frame architecture of the P1P allows convective drafts that rapidly cool the high-shrinkage ASA matrix.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Install an enclosure or cardboard draft shield, set the bed temperature to 98°C, disable auxiliary/part cooling fans, and add an 8mm outer brim.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clicking and progressive under-extrusion mid-print
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Abrasive carbon fibers have worn or clogged the stock P1P stainless steel nozzle, or filament softened in the cold zone due to heat creep.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Swap to a Bambu Hardened Steel 0.4mm hotend assembly and hardened extruder gear kit, and confirm hotend cooling fan is running at 100%.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Brittle parts and poor Z-axis layer bonding
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive cooling fan speed or printing below the optimal polymer melting threshold of 265°C.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase nozzle temperature to 270°C, disable the auxiliary cooling fan entirely, and restrict maximum part cooling fan to 15%.

faq.question: Can I print Bambu ASA-CF on a stock P1P without upgrading the nozzle?
faq.answer: No. The stock P1P comes with a stainless steel nozzle and unhardened gears, which will rapidly erode within a single spool of carbon fiber filament; you must upgrade to a hardened steel hotend and hardened extruder gears.

faq.question: Is an enclosure strictly necessary for printing ASA-CF on the P1P?
faq.answer: While small, low-profile parts may succeed without an enclosure if ambient air is warm and draft-free, structural or tall parts will almost certainly warp or delaminate without a draft shield or full enclosure.

faq.question: Does Bambu ASA-CF need to be dried before printing?
faq.answer: Yes. Even though ASA absorbs less water than nylon, moisture in ASA-CF causes rough surface finish, nozzle foaming, and layer embrittlement; dry it in a filament dryer at 80°C for 8 hours prior to printing.

faq.question: Why use glue stick on a textured PEI plate with ASA-CF?
faq.answer: ASA can chemically bond too aggressively to PEI surfaces at 95-100°C; the glue stick acts as an essential release interface to prevent tearing off the PEI coating when removing parts.
